questions.stem: You are asked to construct a triangle with sides $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$, and $9\text{ cm}$. After drawing the base of $9\text{ cm}$, what compass width should you use from one end?

options.text: $5\text{ cm}$ or $7\text{ cm}$ (one from each end)

questions.explanation: Set the compass to $5\text{ cm}$ and draw an arc from one end, then set it to $7\text{ cm}$ and draw an arc from the other end (or vice versa). The intersection of the arcs gives the third vertex.

questions.stem: To construct a perpendicular to a line from a point not on the line, the first step is to:

options.text: Measure the distance from the point to the line with a ruler
Draw arcs from the point that cross the line at two points
Draw a parallel line through the point

questions.explanation: Place the compass point at the given point and draw an arc that crosses the line at two points. Then construct the perpendicular bisector of the segment between those two crossing points.

questions.stem: Why must construction lines (arcs) be left visible in your work?

options.text: They make the diagram look more complete
They show that the construction was done accurately using compasses, not measured
They are needed to calculate angles
They are only needed for decoration

questions.explanation: Construction arcs must remain visible as evidence that the construction was carried out accurately using compasses and a ruler, rather than by measuring with a protractor.
